newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA GOVERNMENT SUPPORT RISES IN LATEST POLL.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA GOVERNMENT SUPPORT RISES IN LATEST POLL.

text.p: Support for Australia's conservative government has increased, but its lead over the Labor opposition remains steady, according to a newspaper poll published on Tuesday.

The Liberal-National coalition's rating increased one point to 43 percent over the past two weeks, while Labor's support also increased one point to 37 percent, The Australian newspaper's Newspoll found.

Prime Minister John Howard's rating as preferred prime minister fell one point to 42 percent and opposition leader Kim Beazley's remained steady at 29 percent. The poll also found 29 percent of those surveyed were uncommitted.
Support for populist politician Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party fell one point to six percent.
But the recently-formed party remains the third strongest after the traditionally dominant coalition and Labor.

The latest Newspoll measure of primary support compares with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 1996 election that saw Howard sweep into office and end 13 years of Labor rule.
The latest poll surveyed 1,150 voters around the country by telephone over the last weekend.
